newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No change to WAPET oil as cyclone fades.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No change to WAPET oil as cyclone fades.

text.p: Production at the Barrow Island and Thevenard Island oil fields off Western Australia were unaffected by cyclone Ophelia, which forced the shut down of the Griffin offshore field on Tuesday, West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) said on Wednesday.
"We haven't shut down," a WAPET spokesman told Reuters.
The Bureau of Meteorology said it expected to downgrade Ophelia to a tropical low by 1100 GMT on Wednesday.
At its strongest, Ophelia probably reached wind speeds of about 170 km an hour, a Bureau spokesman said.
Barrow produces about 15,000 barrels of oil per day and Thevenard produces some 30,000 bpd, the spokesman said.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.

The Griffin floating oil platform has started its return journey to its production site offshore of Western Australia after disconnecting on Tuesday to avoid the cyclone, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said earlier on Wednesday.
BHP holds 45 percent of Griffin and is the operator.
Mobil Exploration and Producing Australia holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd owns the remaining 20 percent.
